name: Greenstone and Caples Tracks
region: Greenstone and Caples conservation areas, Otago
why: Up the narrow, forested Caples valley, over the boardwalked McKellar Saddle, and back down the wide tussock flats of the Greenstone: a quieter loop next to the Routeburn.
book: Book the DOC huts (Mid Caples, McKellar, Greenstone) or the campsites beside them all year; Upper Caples and Mid Greenstone huts are booked through the NZ Deerstalkers' Association. The road end is 86 km from Queenstown via Glenorchy; the last 11 km from Kinloch is gravel with fords.
water: Hut taps are untreated: boil or treat. Plenty of streams.
dangers: Side streams flood after heavy rain, above all the Caples above Upper Caples Hut and Jean Batten Creek: carry extra food and wait in a hut.
Cattle, including bulls, on the private valley floors: stay on the track at the forest edge.
Avalanche danger around Slip Flat in the lower Greenstone in winter.
Slips between the Caples-Greenstone confluence and Mid Caples Hut: take care in bad weather.
turnaround: If rain is forecast for the McKellar Saddle day, stay at Mid Caples Hut or walk out the way you came.

points.name: Greenstone car park
points.note: End of Greenstone Road by Lake Wakatipu. The Greenstone was a pounamu route for Ngāi Tahu travelling to the West Coast. Keep to the true left of the Caples River.

points.name: Mid Caples Hut
points.note: First night, 9 km and 2-3 h in, just after a gorge. 24 bunks.

points.name: McKellar Saddle
points.note: 945 m, boardwalked over the subalpine bog, at the end of a 22 km day. No camping on the saddle.

points.name: McKellar Hut
points.note: Second night at the south end of Lake McKellar, an hour from the junction below the saddle.

points.name: Greenstone Hut
points.note: Third night, 18 km down the open Greenstone valley past Steele Creek; across a bridge over a gorge.

points.name: Greenstone car park
points.note: 12 km through the Greenstone gorge and Slip Flat, with deep river pools, to the confluence and back to the car park.
